small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_N (e.g. 512) paired with BLOCK_OC=16 and BLOCK_K=48 (full K_TOTAL=27 fits in one iteration, eliminating the K-loop entirely) — since IC*KD*KH*KW=27 here, setting BLOCK_K=32 with a single iteration is ideal and removes loop overhead.
- Try BLOCK_OC=16 (==OC) so the OC tile dimension is exact and the OC grid is 1; sweep BLOCK_N in {128, 256, 512, 1024} with num_warps in {4, 8} and num_stages in {2, 3} to find the bandwidth sweet spot for the gather-heavy inner loop.
- Reorder the grid so pid_n_block is axis 0 (largest dim) and pid_batch is axis 1 for better L2 reuse of the weight tile across batches sharing the same OC tile; or swap to a 2D grid with (N*n_blocks, oc_blocks).
large_guidance:
- Switch to an implicit-GEMM with channels-last (NDHWC) input layout: reshape input to [N*OD*OH*OW, IC*KD*KH*KW] implicitly and weight to [OC, IC*KD*KH*KW]. With K_TOTAL=27 and OC=16, GEMM tiles are tiny — instead consider a direct-conv kernel where each program computes one (n, oh_tile, ow_tile) block across all OC simultaneously, holding the full 16×27 weight in registers/shared memory once per program.
- Persistent kernel: launch one program per SM, loop over (batch, spatial tile) work items so the 16×3×3×3 weight tensor (1728 floats) is loaded into shared memory exactly once per SM and reused across all output positions.
- Alternative: precompute im2col into a workspace once (small, since K_TOTAL=27) and call a tuned GEMM + fused epilogue kernel — but the gather is cheap enough that a direct conv with weight broadcast and BLOCK_OW × BLOCK_OH spatial tiling (reusing input halos across KH/KW) will likely beat im2col-GEMM at these shapes.
